intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about St. Francis County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of County Clerk. Additionally, an issue came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report. County Clerk The county failed to publish financial statements by March 15th, in noncompliance with Ark. Code.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited. The letter continues in the report on page 3; parts that concern staff positions are left to the report, since this site doesn’t single out non-elected staff.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated October 15, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Madison
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor, Recorder/Treasurer and District Court Clerk. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer Although Schedule 1 of this report shows a General Fund balance of $132,790 it was brought to our attention that as of December 31, 2024, the General Fund owed a significant amount for balances owed to the Street and Sanitation Funds. As shown in Note 6 on Schedule 3, when these outstanding amounts were considered, the General Fund had a deficit balance of $235,286. A similar finding was noted in the previous five reports.
